question: Ashok bought some pencils at the rate of ₹180 a dozen. He sold them for ₹16 each. His profit percentage is ______%.
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Cost Price (CP) of 12 pencils = ₹180.

Cost Price (CP) of 1 pencil = 180 ÷ 12 = ₹15.

Selling Price (SP) of 1 pencil = ₹16.

Profit = SP − CP = 16 − 15 = ₹1.

Profit% = (Profit ÷ CP) × 100 = (1 ÷ 15) × 100 = 6.67%.

**∴ The correct answer is 6.67%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** CP of 1 dozen = ₹180 | SP of 1 pencil = ₹16.
**Formulas:** CP per unit = Total CP ÷ Quantity | Profit = SP − CP | Profit% = (Profit ÷ CP) × 100.
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/55a969fc44e535d3a9b1c687665baf2a9c9b818cf1fac6e219dd71d0f7a62929.png] 
⇒ **Cost Price (CP)** of 12 pencils = ₹180.
⇒ **Cost Price (CP)** of 1 pencil = 180 ÷ 12 = ₹15.
⇒ **Selling Price (SP)** of 1 pencil = ₹16.
⇒ **Profit** = 16 − 15 = ₹1.
⇒ **Profit Percentage** = (1 ÷ 15) × 100 = 20 ÷ 3 = 6.666...% ≈ 6.67%.

**∴ The correct answer is 6.67%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Unit Calculation

Always ensure that the **Cost Price** and **Selling Price** are calculated for the same number of units to find the correct profit or loss percentage.

Profit and Loss Percent

Profit% and Loss% are always calculated on the **Cost Price (CP)** unless stated otherwise in the question.
